title: It Is Not My Code Anymore
abstract: arXiv:2609.09022v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI-assisted programming raises distinct questions about who produces code, who feels ownership of it, and who is responsible when it fails. This research note examines these distinctions through a hypothetical enrollment failure and a selective reading of the literature. Identifying the producer of a defective expression does not, by itself, determine the duties of reviewers, release decision-makers, or service operators. Collective ownership likewise leaves those duties to be specified. The discussion then considers how quality engineering can evaluate both generated implementations and the processes that produce them. Acceptance criteria should be justified by the required service outcome, with component checks contributing evidence toward that outcome. translated_abstract: AI辅助编程引发了一系列独特的问题：代码由谁编写、谁对其拥有归属感、以及当代码失效时谁应当承担责任。本研究笔记通过一个假设性的选课系统故障案例以及对文献的选择性解读来考察这些区别。确定有缺陷的表达由谁编写，本身并不能决定审查者、发布决策者或服务运营者的职责；同样，集体所有权模式也未能明确这些职责。随后，讨论转向质量工程如何同时评估生成的代码实现以及产生这些实现的过程。验收标准应当以所需的服务结果为依据进行论证，而组件检查则作为支持该结果的证据。这一视角还允许与那些直接执行任务而不生成独立程序的系统进行比较。这种替代方式将改变创作归属的对象，同时……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文指出AI辅助编程中代码的作者身份、所有权与责任归属是相互独立的问题，并主张应通过以服务结果为依据的验收标准和质量工程方法，来同时评估AI生成的代码及其生成过程。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that in AI-assisted programming, authorship, ownership, and responsibility are distinct notions, and proposes that quality engineering should evaluate both AI-generated implementations and the processes producing them against acceptance criteria justified by the required service outcomes.
